title: Skill Failure Mode Classifier
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Classification activity in which learners attribute eight illustrative observations of a misbehaving agent skill, in a fixed order, to one of six failure modes: undertriggering, overtriggering, instruction drift, missing dependency, stale reference, and scope creep. Each observation gets one attempt, followed by Correct or This is <mode> with a one-sentence reason. The run ends with a score out of 8, a mastery statement at 7 of 8, and the recommended fix for each mode that was missed.

educational.topic: Diagnosing agent skill failures by symptom
learningObjectives: Attribute each of eight observed skill problems to one of six failure modes, with at least 7 of 8 correct
Name the recommended fix for each failure mode
prerequisites: The six skill failure modes: undertriggering, overtriggering, instruction drift, missing dependency, stale reference, and scope creep

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; the drop-down list and the button are native HTML controls reachable with the Tab key; the selected, correct, and wrong modes are marked with an arrow, a check mark, and an X as well as a color-blind-safe blue and vermillion outline; text is 16 px, reduced to no less than 14 px only at narrow widths.

controls.label: Failure mode
controls.purpose: Chooses one of the six failure modes for the current observation. Disabled after the choice is submitted.

controls.label: Submit / Next Observation / See Score
controls.purpose: Submit commits the chosen mode (one attempt per observation). After submission the button advances to the next observation, and after observation 8 it shows the score.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Six-way attribution of symptoms to causes with immediate explanatory feedback and targeted fixes for missed modes
keyQuestions: Did the skill load at all, and should it have?
If it loaded, what was skipped, missing, outdated, or added?
commonMisconceptions: Any skill problem is a problem with the model
A skill that gives a wrong answer must have bad instructions
A skill that does not run has failed to trigger
assessmentOpportunities: At least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
Learner explains how the recommended fix for each missed mode addresses its cause
